set_aside.subject: AuditRecord occurred_at
set_aside.text: M37 says “audit_writer supplies audit_id and occurred_at; callers cannot supply either,” while A28 says “Each operation reads the clock once” and that one instant supplies every portal-owned timestamp it writes.
set_aside.question: How does audit_writer obtain the owning operation’s single instant without reading the clock a second time or accepting occurred_at from its caller?
options: audit_writer reads the clock, potentially producing a different instant from the business records
the owning use case passes the operation instant separately, despite callers being forbidden to supply occurred_at
audit_writer supplies the instant to the owning use case before any records are built
set_aside.default_guess: Pass the operation’s already-read instant to audit_writer as a non-AuditIntent argument.

witness.initial: An active project contains an expense that an authorized operator may correct.
events: The owning use case reads time T1 and builds the replacement Expense with updated_at=T1.
The use case asks audit_writer to append expense.correct.
outcomes: audit_writer reads time again and writes occurred_at=T2, so the business change and its audit have different portal-owned instants.
The use case passes T1 to audit_writer despite M37, so both records use T1.
witness.observer: An administrator or test reading the Expense and AuditRecord timestamps.

set_aside.subject: Rejected significant mutations
set_aside.text: M36 says “every significant action … writes exactly one record” and requires a reason for a rejected significant mutation, while A13 and State 3 say “Every other refused operation rolls its transaction back and writes no record” except snapshot.import and staff.login_failed.
set_aside.question: Does a refused significant mutation other than snapshot.import produce a rejected AuditRecord or no AuditRecord?
options: write one rejected AuditRecord for every refused significant mutation as M36 states
write no record for such refusals except snapshot.import, as A13 and State 3 state
set_aside.default_guess: Follow the later accepted A13 rule and write no record except for snapshot.import and staff.login_failed.

witness.initial: An expense exists in a project that Registry now reports archived.
events: Authorization refuses the mutation because the project is archived.
The audit log is read afterward.
outcomes: M36 yields one expense.correct record with result=rejected and an archived-project reason.
A13 and State 3 yield no audit record for the refused correction.
witness.observer: An administrator, auditor, or audit test.

set_aside.subject: staff.login_failed actor provenance
set_aside.text: A13 requires staff.login_failed records, but M36 permits only staff, viewer, service, or system actors and requires actor_id unless actor_kind=system; a failed login may use an email that identifies no StaffAccount.
set_aside.question: What actor_kind and actor_id must audit_writer accept for staff.login_failed when authentication resolves no staff account, and must known-account and unknown-account failures use the same representation?
options: always record actor_kind=system with no actor_id
record actor_kind=staff with staff_id when an account is resolved and system otherwise
do not record failures for unknown accounts
set_aside.default_guess: Use actor_kind=system with no actor_id for every failed login so the audit shape does not depend on account existence.

events: An external caller submits a staff login using nobody@example.test and an arbitrary password.
authenticate_staff rejects the login and asks audit_writer to append staff.login_failed.
outcomes: The failure is recorded as a system action with no actor_id.
No record is written because a required staff actor_id does not exist, or the implementation uses a different actor representation for unknown accounts.
witness.observer: An administrator or audit-log consumer; the difference can also disclose internally whether an email resolved to an account.

set_aside.subject: AuditIntent entity_kind and entity_id
set_aside.text: audit_writer owns validation against A13 and A23, but the texts define no action-to-AuditEntityKind/entity_id compatibility table; they only say the owning use case builds the intent and that entity_id is the audited entity’s canonical identifier.
set_aside.question: Which entity_kind and identifier are valid for each AuditAction, and does audit_writer validate that semantic pairing or merely validate the identifier’s UUID syntax?
options: audit_writer owns and enforces a closed action-to-entity mapping
each use case chooses the affected entity and audit_writer checks only generic shape and canonical UUID syntax
multiple entity kinds are valid for an action under an explicitly listed per-action rule
set_aside.default_guess: Define and enforce a closed action-to-entity mapping in audit_writer, using the newly created or mutated entity unless a stated exception applies.

witness.initial: An active viewer exists and has no current access credential.
events: The viewer_access use case builds the viewer.credential_issue AuditIntent.
outcomes: The record names entity_kind=viewer_credential and the new credential_id.
The record names entity_kind=viewer and the viewer_id; both are canonical UUIDs and both entities are affected by the issue operation.
witness.observer: An administrator or audit consumer following the audit reference to determine what was issued.
